How do I get started?

• Create a profile.
• Choose what you want to block or limit.
• Enable Switchly.

Optional: require NFC/QR to disable, so you can’t turn it off too easily in weak moments.
How does Switchly work (in a nutshell)?
Switchly helps you stay focused by blocking apps, websites, and specific in-app areas (like Shorts/Reels). You choose rules per profile, then Switchly enforces them while it is enabled.
What does the tutorial do?
The tutorial reopens the setup walkthrough: permissions, profile basics, and core features (NFC/QR, schedules, limits). It does not delete your data; it only guides you through setup again.
Can I change the app language?
Yes. Go to Settings → General → Language.\nThe app restarts for the change to take effect.
Does Switchly support dark mode?
Yes. Choose Light, Dark, or System in Settings → General → Theme.\nPremium unlocks additional colors and a custom color picker.
How do I use Switchly in a nutshell?
Create one profile, choose what should be blocked, enable Switchly, done. If you want extra friction, enable NFC/QR unlock so you cannot disable it too easily in weak moments.
What features does Switchly have?
Core features: app blocking, website blocking, in-app blocking (like Shorts/Reels/Explore), blocked notifications inbox, profiles, schedules, limits, usage stats, and backup/restore (when signed in).
In-app blocking (YouTube/Instagram) – how it works

In-app blocking uses Accessibility to detect specific screens (e.g., YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels/Explore) and redirect you out of them. If a popup does not always appear, it can be due to navigation timing or app UI changes; Switchly still attempts to exit the blocked area safely.
Blocked websites – what happens

Website blocking applies to pages opened in supported browsers while Switchly is active. If a domain is blocked, Switchly prevents loading and can show a blocked screen depending on your settings.\nFirefox note: support can vary by app/browser version because URL bars and view IDs change. If Chrome works but Firefox does not, update to the latest beta build and report your device + Firefox version so we can adjust detection.
Blocked notifications – what is stored
Blocked notifications are saved only on your device. Tap an entry to see full details such as app, time, reason, title, message, and additional fields (if available).
What are profiles for?
Profiles contain app selections and blocking rules, e.g., “Work”, “Study”, or “Sleep”.\nYou can create, rename, duplicate, or delete profiles.\nThe active profile is always shown at the top.
Why did my NFC tag stop working after renaming a profile?

NFC tags store the profile name in plain text.
If you rename or delete that profile, the tag no longer matches.

Rewrite the NFC tag with the updated name to fix this.
What is the difference between “Temporary disable” and “Emergency unlock”?

Temporary disable pauses blocking for a short time (e.g., 10 minutes) and then enables it again automatically. You can use it as often as you want.

Emergency unlock disables all restrictions for a fixed time (e.g., 15 minutes) and can only be used once per calendar day to prevent overuse.
Both timers are shown on the main screen.
What is “Temporary enable”?
This lets you enable blocking for a limited time. When the timer ends, Switchly automatically restores the previous state.
What is “Re-entry” in NFC write?

Re-entry writes an NFC action that temporarily disables Switchly for the selected duration (for example 10 minutes), so you can enter settings and adjust things.\nAfter the timer ends, the previous state is restored automatically.\nTo show Re-entry in the NFC writer, enable “Enable Re-entry in NFC writer” in Toggle Options.
Can I write an “Emergency disable” NFC tag?

No — Emergency disable tags were removed to reduce bypass loops. Emergency unlock is now only available from inside the app.
If you want stricter control for NFC tags, enable “Limit temporary disable NFC tags” in Toggle Options.
That adds per-tag cooldown and daily limits for Temporary disable and Re-entry tags.
You can set custom limits per UID in Manage Paired Tags. First enable “Enable paired NFC tags” in Toggle Options, then open Manage Paired Tags and tap a tag to edit Daily uses and Cooldown minutes.
What does “Require NFC tag to disable” do?

When enabled, Switchly can only be disabled by scanning a valid NFC tag.

Manual toggle, Quick Settings tile, and certain controls are locked or show warnings.
This acts like a physical “key” to turn off your restriction profile.
What does Emergency unlock do?
Emergency unlock disables all blocking for a short time (e.g., 15 minutes).\nIt can only be used once per calendar day. After it ends, Switchly automatically resumes blocking.
Why are some settings grayed out or show a toast?

Some settings are intentionally disabled while protection is active. Most common reasons:
• Switchly is currently enabled
• NFC/QR unlock is required
• A temporary timer/lock is active
• A required permission is missing

This anti-bypass behavior is intentional. If you need to edit critical options, unlock/disable first and then try again.
Why are some settings grayed out?
Because protection is active. If Switchly is enabled/locked (especially with NFC/QR unlock), critical settings are intentionally disabled to prevent bypassing. Unlock/disable first, then edit.
Using NFC + QR together
You can enable both. This means disabling Switchly requires the allowed method(s) you configured. Pick what fits your setup (e.g., NFC at home + QR as backup).
How do I use NFC + QR together?
Use NFC as your main method and QR as backup. Keep the QR less convenient (e.g., in a drawer or wallet) so it still helps against impulsive disabling.
How do NFC tags work with Switchly?

Switchly can write NFC tags that trigger actions instantly:

• Global actions: enable, disable, toggle, or temporarily disable (e.g., 10 minutes)
• Profile actions: activate a specific profile and then enable, disable, or toggle

If the profile on a tag no longer exists, Switchly shows a toast and does nothing.
Most standard NDEF-compatible tags are supported; only proprietary formats may fail.
How to use Switchly with NFC
Open the NFC writer and write a Switchly trigger to an NFC tag. If NFC-required unlock is enabled, you will need to scan a valid tag to disable Switchly.
What is “paired tags/UID-only”?

If enabled, Switchly will only accept NFC tags whose UID you paired. This prevents bypassing with random tags.\nTo manage paired tags, first enable “Enable paired NFC tags” in Toggle Options. After that, “Manage paired tags” becomes available in Settings.
NFC pairing/UID-only mode

UID-only mode is a security feature: when enabled, Switchly only accepts NFC tags whose UID you paired.
If you accidentally paired a transit card or another tag UID, other tags may be rejected with “Wrong NFC tag (paired UID required)”.
To remove or rename paired tags, first enable “Enable paired NFC tags” in Toggle Options, then open Manage Paired Tags in Settings.
Pairing is done by scanning a tag in the NFC writer and choosing “Pair UID”.
What does “Pair tag (UID only)” do?

“Pair tag (UID only)” does not write anything to the NFC tag.
Instead, Switchly only reads the tag UID (hardware ID) and stores it inside the app.

If UID pairing is enabled, only that exact tag can be used to toggle or unlock Switchly.
This is useful for read-only tags or if you do not want the tag to contain a readable action.
Which NFC tag types work?

Best compatibility: NTAG213, NTAG215, NTAG216 (NFC Forum Type 2). In general, most writable NDEF-capable tags work. Avoid locked read-only tags for writing. UID-only pairing also works with tags you cannot write to.
How does NFC work with Switchly?

Switchly reads an NFC tag trigger. You write or pair a tag once, then scanning that tag can perform protected actions (for example unlock or disable, depending on your setup). UID-only mode accepts only paired tag IDs for extra security.
What are QR actions?
Switchly can save actions (e.g., switching profiles or toggling modes) as a QR code. You can share or print it.
How do I create a QR code?
Open the QR screen, choose the action/profile, then tap “Create”. You can save or share the code afterward.
How do I scan a QR code?
Open the QR scanner in Switchly and point the camera at the code. The action is executed immediately.
How to use Switchly with QR
Create a QR trigger in the app and print/save it. If “QR required” is enabled, you must scan the QR code to disable Switchly.
How to use Switchly with NFC (step by step)

1. Open the NFC writer.
2. Hold the tag to your phone and write it.
3. Optional: use “Pair UID” if you want UID-only security.
4. If you want only paired tags to work, enable “Enable paired NFC tags” in Toggle Options.
How to use Switchly with QR (step by step)

1. Create a QR trigger in Switchly.
2. Print it or keep it on another device/location.
3. Enable QR unlock as required.
4. Scan this QR code when you need to unlock or disable.
Which NFC tags are recommended?
Recommended: NTAG213, NTAG215, NTAG216 (best compatibility). NTAG213 is enough for most users. Buy from a reliable seller and avoid random ultra-cheap no-name packs.
How do schedules work?

Schedules let Switchly react automatically when a condition matches.

A schedule has two parts:
• Condition: when it should become active (time, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth)
• Action: what Switchly should do when that happens

Examples:
• Time schedule: every weekday from 08:00 to 16:00
• Wi-Fi schedule: while connected to your work network
• Bluetooth schedule: when your car device is connected

Some actions only trigger once, while others stay in effect for the whole active period and revert when the schedule ends.
What does the schedule “Action” do?

Each schedule action controls what happens when the schedule becomes active:

• Enable: Turns Switchly on when the schedule starts. It stays on until something else changes it.
• Disable: Turns Switchly off when the schedule starts. It stays off until something else changes it.
• Toggle: Flips the current state once when the schedule triggers.
• Enable & Disable: Turns Switchly on while the schedule is active, then turns it off again when the schedule ends.
• Disable & Enable: Turns Switchly off while the schedule is active, then turns it on again when the schedule ends.

Range-style actions are best when you want a schedule to control both start and end. One-shot actions are better when the schedule should only trigger once.
What schedule types can I use?

Switchly supports time schedules (single time/range/date range), Wi-Fi schedules (SSID), and Bluetooth schedules (device name). You can choose actions like Enable, Disable, Toggle, or Enable+Disable depending on your use case.
Why do Wi-Fi schedules need Location permission?

Android treats the Wi-Fi name (SSID) as location-like information.
On newer versions, apps need Location permission to read the current SSID.

Without it, Wi-Fi schedules cannot reliably detect your current network and may not trigger.
Can schedules react to Bluetooth?
Yes. You can trigger actions when a specific Bluetooth device connects/disconnects (depending on schedule options).
How do app limits work?
If you set a daily limit, Switchly tracks usage time and blocks the app once the limit is reached.
Where can I set a daily limit?
In the app picker, tap the timer/limit icon next to an app, then choose a preset or “Custom”.
How do I remove a limit?
Set the limit to “No limit”. Then the time cap will no longer be enforced.
What does “Overall” mean in usage statistics?

Overall sums all saved usage data since you started using Switchly (based on locally stored daily values). If you cleared app data or restored an older backup, Overall reflects the currently stored state.
Why does Switchly need Accessibility?

Switchly uses an Accessibility service to detect when you open a blocked app (window/app changes). It only reacts to those events to enforce your profiles. No keystrokes are recorded, and Switchly does not store your screen contents.
Where does usage data come from?
Switchly uses Android’s Usage Access permission to detect the foreground app and estimate usage time.
Do I need the overlay permission?

No. Newer versions of Switchly do not require overlay permission. Blocking is handled via Accessibility and a full-screen blocker. If you granted overlay in an older version, you can safely revoke it in system settings.
Why does Switchly behave differently on my device?
Some manufacturers restrict APIs that affect overlays, background services, or Quick Settings tiles.\nSwitchly uses only official APIs — behavior still depends on your device/ROM settings.
Does Switchly use a lot of battery?

Switchly is event-based: the Accessibility service reacts when apps change, so there is no constant polling. Battery impact is typically low. If you use Wi-Fi/Bluetooth schedules, Android may show an ongoing notification because those features require foreground services on many devices.
What data does Switchly collect?
All processing happens locally on your device. No usage data or personal information is sent externally.\nAny future cloud features will be optional and clearly explained.
What exactly does Switchly Premium include?

Switchly Premium adds optional features, while core blocking stays free.

You get:
• More accent colors and a custom color picker
• Custom temporary lock and unlock durations
• Additional Wi-Fi and Bluetooth schedules
• Enhanced insights and statistics
How do I get Premium?
Open Settings → Premium. There you can view features and unlock Premium via Google Play Billing. If a purchase is delayed, open the Premium screen again to refresh your status.
What about usage statistics or analytics?
Some analytics may be part of Premium — optional and privacy-friendly.\nThey help you understand habits and improve the app.\nNo tracking across other apps or services.
How do I save my data (backup/restore)?
Sign in first, then open Settings → Account/Cloud backup and create a backup. On a new device (or after reset), sign in with the same account and use Restore to load a backup.
How do I delete my account?
Open Settings → Google account → Delete account. This removes your Switchly cloud account data. If you also want a clean phone state, run “Delete all Switchly data” in the in-app reset.
How do I add the Quick Settings tile?
Enable “Quick Settings tile availability” in Toggle Options, then open Android’s Quick Settings editor and add “Switchly”.\nOn some devices, the tile or its label may appear with a slight delay.
Why is the Quick Settings tile missing?
First enable “Quick Settings tile availability” in Toggle Options, then add the tile from Android’s Quick Settings edit screen.\nSome OEMs only show tiles after the app has been opened once.

Is there a simpler version of Switchly too?

Yep, there is also Switchly Lite as a lighter option for simple blocking flows like NFC, button actions, and timed schedules. Think of it as a more stripped-back version of Switchly with fewer advanced features.
What are protection controls / control mode?

Protection controls decide which paths are allowed to enable or disable Switchly.

Depending on the selected control mode, Switchly can accept changes from schedules, NFC tags, QR actions, or manual controls like the home toggle button and Quick Settings tile.

This is not just about unlocking. It defines which control channels are trusted at all.
What is Schedule mode?

Schedule mode focuses on automatic routines.
Only schedules are allowed to control Switchly automatically.
NFC and QR actions are ignored while this mode is active.

Use this when your setup should follow time, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth conditions instead of physical tags or QR codes.
What is NFC mode?

NFC mode focuses on physical friction.
Only NFC actions are accepted for automation.
Schedules and QR actions are ignored while this mode is active.

This is useful if you want a physical tag to be the main control method.
What is QR mode?

QR mode focuses on QR-based workflows.
Only QR actions are accepted for automation.
Schedules and NFC actions are ignored while this mode is active.

Use this if your unlock or toggle flow should depend on scanning a QR code.
What is Mixed mode?

Mixed mode is the flexible option.
Instead of allowing only one control path, you can choose exactly which channels are allowed.

That means you can allow any combination of schedules, NFC, QR, and manual controls.
For example, you could allow schedules and NFC, but block QR and manual buttons.
What are manual controls?

Manual controls are the direct controls inside the app or system UI.
This usually includes the home toggle button, other manual buttons, and the Quick Settings tile.

If manual controls are blocked by the current control mode, those buttons may be disabled, ignored, or show a warning instead of changing Switchly.
